description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. Before the list is reviewed, a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image. After review, it removes an old stopped container that nothing protects, and keeps, with their images, stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep. With Docker restarted under extra daemon flags each time: a --log-driver=journald daemon and a --log-opt daemon get no log-opts in daemon.json and still start; a --log-driver=json-file daemon gets them and starts with them; a stopped daemon's flags are read from docker.service and its environment file, and flags it cannot resolve skip log rotation with exit 3; a daemon.json an earlier version already broke is reported as DAEMON WILL NOT START, exit 3, unchanged, and Docker really does fail to start with it. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2.

steps.label: Record daemon.json as it was before the component
steps.run: mkdir -p /etc/docker; if [ -s /etc/docker/daemon.json ]; then cp /etc/docker/daemon.json /tmp/tc-before.json; else echo '{}' > /tmp/tc-before.json; fi; cat /tmp/tc-before.json

steps.label: Report mode
Report mode changed nothing
steps.run: test ! -e /etc/systemd/system/tc-docker-prune.timer && test ! -e /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers && { cmp -s /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json || { test ! -s /etc/docker/daemon.json && test "$(cat /tmp/tc-before.json)" = '{}'; }; }

steps.label: Apply
daemon.json carries the limits
Every key that was already there is unchanged
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open('/tmp/tc-before.json')); b=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); bad=[k for k in a if b.get(k)!=a[k] and k not in ('log-opts','builder')]; print('changed:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

steps.label: dockerd accepts the new file
steps.run: dockerd --validate --config-file /etc/docker/daemon.json

steps.label: Prune timer enabled and scheduled
steps.run: systemctl is-enabled tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl is-active tc-docker-prune.timer && systemctl list-timers tc-docker-prune.timer --no-pager

steps.label: Prune script has an age filter and never prunes volumes
Second run changes nothing
One-off prune, before review: no containers or images touched
The prune service itself runs
steps.run: systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service && systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value

steps.label: Expected list created, with its header
Ignore file created with an example
Settings file carries only the age
Stopped containers: one listed, one unless-stopped, one tc.keep, one unprotected
steps.run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $d/bin; cp /bin/sleep /bin/true $d/bin/; for l in $(ldd /bin/sleep | grep -oE '/[^ ]+'); do mkdir -p $d$(dirname $l); cp $l $d$l; done; for t in listed policy labelled junk; do tar -C $d -c . | docker import --change "LABEL tc.test=$t" - tc-test-$t:1; done; echo name:tc-listed >> /etc/tc-docker/expected-containers; docker create --name tc-listed tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true; docker run -d --name tc-policy --restart unless-stopped tc-test-policy:1 /bin/sleep 3600; docker stop -t 1 tc-policy; docker create --name tc-labelled --label tc.keep=true tc-test-labelled:1 /bin/true; docker create --name tc-junk tc-test-junk:1 /bin/true; docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}}' | grep tc-test; docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.label: A later run never rewrites the list
The hand-added entry is still on the list
Before review: a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image
steps.run: sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune && systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 40 --no-pager; docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} survived' tc-junk; docker image inspect -f 'junk image survived' tc-test-junk:1

steps.label: Record a review, as Update Expected Containers' Confirm reviewed does
steps.run: echo 'tc-test review' > /etc/tc-docker/reviewed && cat /etc/tc-docker/reviewed

steps.label: A later run reports the list as reviewed
After review: prune with no age limit, run by the timer's service
steps.run: docker inspect -f 'before: {{.Name}} present' tc-junk; docker ps -a --format 'before: {{.Names}} {{.Status}}'; sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=0/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune && systemctl start tc-docker-prune.service; systemctl show tc-docker-prune.service -p Result --value; journalctl -u tc-docker-prune.service -n 40 --no-pager; docker ps -a --format 'after: {{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

steps.label: Protected containers and their images survived; the unprotected ones did not
steps.run: for c in tc-listed tc-policy tc-labelled; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} kept' $c; done; for i in listed policy labelled; do docker image inspect -f "image tc-test-$i kept" tc-test-$i:1; done; docker inspect tc-junk >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'tc-junk STILL HERE' || echo 'tc-junk removed'; docker image inspect tc-test-junk:1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'junk image STILL HERE' || echo 'junk image removed'

steps.label: Refuses a bad log size
Refuses a prune age under 24 hours
Refuses a schedule systemd cannot parse
Daemon flags: set up a helper that restarts Docker with extra dockerd flags through a docker.service drop-in
steps.run: set -e; systemctl show docker.service -p ExecStart --value | sed -n 's/.*argv\[\]=\([^;]*\) ;.*/\1/p' | head -n 1 > /tmp/tc-execstart; test -s /tmp/tc-execstart; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# tc-test-docker-flags FLAG...: restart docker.service with these extra dockerd flags (a drop-in).' 'd=/etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d' 'mkdir -p "$d"' '{ echo "[Service]"; echo "EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/tc-test-docker"; echo "ExecStart="; echo "ExecStart=$(cat /tmp/tc-execstart) $*"; } > "$d/tc-test.conf"' 'systemctl daemon-reload' 'systemctl reset-failed docker.service docker.socket 2>/dev/null' 'if systemctl restart docker.service; then' '  for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done' '  echo "docker came up with [$*]: LoggingDriver=$(docker info --format "{{.LoggingDriver}}")"' 'else' '  echo "docker DID NOT START with [$*]"' '  journalctl -u docker.service -n 50 --no-pager | grep -E "failed to start|unable to configure|unknown log opt|specified both" | tail -n 3' '  exit 1' 'fi' > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; echo "docker.service starts: $(cat /tmp/tc-execstart)"

steps.label: Daemon flags: Docker running with --log-driver=journald
steps.run: cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=journald

steps.label: Daemon flags: a --log-driver=journald daemon gets no log rotation
outputContains: Docker starts with --log-driver=journald (read from the running dockerd
SKIPPED: log rotation: log-driver is journald (from the --log-driver flag)
passes dockerd --validate with the daemon's logging flags

steps.label: Daemon flags: journald - daemon.json has no log-opts, and Docker restarts, comes up and runs a container
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); print('daemon.json has log-opts' if 'log-opts' in d else 'daemon.json has no log-opts'); sys.exit(1 if 'log-opts' in d else 0)" && tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=journald && docker run -d --name tc-logtest-journald tc-test-listed:1 /bin/sleep 5 >/dev/null && docker inspect -f "tc-logtest-journald LogConfig {{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}" tc-logtest-journald; docker rm -f tc-logtest-journald >/dev/null

steps.label: Daemon flags: Docker running with --log-opt max-size=50m
steps.run: cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && tc-test-docker-flags --log-opt max-size=50m

steps.label: Daemon flags: a daemon with --log-opt gets no log rotation
outputContains: Docker starts with --log-opt max-size (read from the running dockerd
SKIPPED: log rotation: dockerd is started with --log-opt (max-size)

steps.label: Daemon flags: --log-opt - daemon.json has no log-opts, and Docker restarts and keeps the flag's max-size
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); print('daemon.json has log-opts' if 'log-opts' in d else 'daemon.json has no log-opts'); sys.exit(1 if 'log-opts' in d else 0)" && tc-test-docker-flags --log-opt max-size=50m && docker run -d --name tc-logtest-50m tc-test-listed:1 /bin/sleep 5 >/dev/null && docker inspect -f "tc-logtest-50m LogConfig {{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}" tc-logtest-50m; docker rm -f tc-logtest-50m >/dev/null

steps.label: Daemon flags: Docker running with --log-driver=json-file and no --log-opt
steps.run: cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=json-file

steps.label: Daemon flags: --log-driver=json-file still gets log rotation
outputContains: Docker starts with --log-driver=json-file (read from the running dockerd
passes dockerd --validate with the daemon's logging flags

steps.label: Daemon flags: json-file - log-opts added, and after a real restart Docker is up and new containers rotate at 10m
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; o=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')).get('log-opts', {}); print('daemon.json log-opts:', json.dumps(o)); sys.exit(0 if o.get('max-size') == '10m' else 1)" && tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=json-file && docker run -d --name tc-logtest-10m tc-test-listed:1 /bin/sleep 5 >/dev/null && docker inspect -f "tc-logtest-10m LogConfig {{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}" tc-logtest-10m; docker rm -f tc-logtest-10m >/dev/null

steps.label: Daemon flags: Docker stopped; docker.service passes $DOCKER_OPTS=--log-driver=journald from an environment file
steps.run: cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && printf '%s\n' '# test' 'DOCKER_OPTS="--log-driver=journald"' > /etc/default/tc-test-docker && tc-test-docker-flags '$DOCKER_OPTS' && systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; systemctl is-active docker.service || true

steps.label: Daemon flags: stopped Docker - the unit's journald flag is found and log rotation is skipped
outputContains: SKIPPED: log rotation: log-driver is journald (from the --log-driver flag)

steps.label: Daemon flags: stopped Docker - daemon.json has no log-opts, and Docker starts
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); print('daemon.json has log-opts' if 'log-opts' in d else 'daemon.json has no log-opts'); sys.exit(1 if 'log-opts' in d else 0)" && tc-test-docker-flags '$DOCKER_OPTS'

steps.label: Daemon flags: Docker stopped; $DOCKER_OPTS is built from another variable
steps.run: cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && printf '%s\n' 'DOCKER_OPTS="--log-driver=json-file --label=tc-test=$TCX"' > /etc/default/tc-test-docker && tc-test-docker-flags '$DOCKER_OPTS' && systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; systemctl is-active docker.service || true

steps.label: Daemon flags: flags that cannot be determined skip log rotation and exit 3
outputContains: could not tell which flags Docker starts with
SKIPPED: log rotation: Docker's start flags could not be determined

steps.label: Daemon flags: undetermined - daemon.json has no log-opts, and Docker starts
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); print('daemon.json has log-opts' if 'log-opts' in d else 'daemon.json has no log-opts'); sys.exit(1 if 'log-opts' in d else 0)" && tc-test-docker-flags '$DOCKER_OPTS'

steps.label: Daemon flags: a host version 4 broke - journald daemon running, daemon.json given max-size after it started
steps.run: rm -f /etc/default/tc-test-docker && cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=journald && cp -p /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S) && python3 -c "import json; p='/etc/docker/daemon.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d['log-opts']={'max-size': '10m', 'max-file': '3'}; json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'), indent=2)" && sha256sum /etc/docker/daemon.json > /tmp/tc-broken.sha && ls -1 /etc/docker/

steps.label: Daemon flags: the broken host is reported, exit 3, nothing written
outputContains: DAEMON WILL NOT START: daemon.json has log-opts max-size and max-file, but the log driver is journald (from the --log-driver flag), which does not accept them

steps.label: Daemon flags: the broken host's daemon.json is byte-for-byte unchanged
steps.run: sha256sum -c /tmp/tc-broken.sha

steps.label: Daemon flags: and the report was right - Docker really does not start with that file
steps.run: tc-test-docker-flags --log-driver=journald

steps.label: Daemon flags: clean up - original daemon.json, no drop-in, Docker running
steps.run: rm -f /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/tc-test.conf /etc/default/tc-test-docker && cp /tmp/tc-before.json /etc/docker/daemon.json && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl reset-failed docker.service docker.socket; systemctl restart docker.service && docker info --format "docker up, LoggingDriver={{.LoggingDriver}}"

steps.label: After a Docker restart, a new container gets max-size 10m
steps.run: systemctl restart docker && docker run --rm -d --name tc-logtest alpine sleep 30 && docker inspect tc-logtest --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}'

steps.label: Host without Docker says so and exits 0
